authority: District Magistrate / Municipal Corporation / Entertainment Tax Department

description.en: A Cinema License (also called a Theatre License or Cinematograph License) is required for any person operating a cinema hall, multiplex, or any premises where cinematograph exhibitions are held for public entertainment. The license is issued under the Cinematograph Act 1952 and respective state cinemas regulation acts. It involves obtaining multiple clearances including fire safety, structural stability, electrical safety, and health/sanitary certificates.

verifiedConditions.claim: The cinema premises must comply with structural stability requirements, fire safety norms, electrical safety standards, ventilation requirements, and seating capacity limitations as prescribed by the state cinema regulation rules.
The building must have an approved building plan from the local municipal authority and a structural stability certificate from a licensed structural engineer.

unverifiedEligibility: Specific structural and safety norms vary by state and municipality.
Multiplexes may have different requirements than single-screen theatres.
Some states require the applicant to be a resident of the state.
Temporary or touring cinema exhibitions may have separate simplified licensing.

requirements.claim: Prescribed application form for cinema license available from the District Magistrate's office or the state licensing authority.
Approved building plan from the municipal/local planning authority, along with structural stability certificate from a licensed structural engineer.
Fire safety No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Chief Fire Officer or State Fire Service Department, certifying adequate fire prevention and firefighting arrangements.
Electrical safety certificate from the State Electrical Inspector verifying the electrical installations, wiring, earthing, and projection equipment meet safety standards.
Health and sanitary certificate from the Municipal Health Officer verifying adequate sanitary facilities (toilets, drinking water, cleanliness) as per prescribed norms.
Detailed seating plan showing number of seats per class, aisle widths, emergency exit locations, and compliance with prescribed spacing norms between rows.

processInformation.claim: Obtain all prerequisite clearances before applying: fire safety NOC, electrical inspector certificate, structural stability certificate, health/sanitary certificate, and approved building plan.
Submit the application form along with all NOCs, certificates, seating plan, and prescribed fee to the District Magistrate or the designated licensing authority.

A joint inspection is conducted by representatives from fire, electrical, structural, and health departments to verify the premises on-site. Any deficiencies identified must be rectified before the license is granted.
Upon successful inspection, the District Magistrate or licensing authority grants the cinema license. The license is typically valid for one year and must be renewed annually with updated NOCs.

output.claim: A Cinema License is issued containing the licensee's name, address of the cinema premises, seating capacity, classes of seats, validity period, and conditions of operation. The license must be displayed in the cinema premises.

fees.applicability: Cinema license application and annual fee
fees.claim: License fee ranges from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 50,000 depending on the state, location (urban/rural), seating capacity, and whether it is a single screen or multiplex. Annual renewal fees are generally similar.

processingTime.applicability: Cinema license from application to grant
processingTime.claim: Processing typically takes 30-90 days once all prerequisite NOCs are in hand. The time to obtain individual NOCs (fire, electrical, structural, health) is additional and can take several weeks each. Total elapsed time from starting the process to license grant is typically 3-6 months.

sources.title: Cinematograph Act 1952 and State Cinema Regulation Acts
sources.publisher: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India / State Governments
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Cinematograph Act 1952 provides the central framework for regulating cinema exhibitions. Section 10 empowers the District Magistrate to grant licenses for cinema premises. State-specific cinema regulation acts and rules prescribe detailed safety, structural, and operational requirements.
claimsSupported: Cinema license is mandatory under the Cinematograph Act 1952.
Fire safety, electrical safety, structural stability, and health certificates are prerequisites.
District Magistrate is the licensing authority.
License is typically annual and requires renewal with updated NOCs.
sources.uncertainty: The Cinematograph (Amendment) Act 2023 introduced changes to certification and anti-piracy provisions but licensing remains with state authorities.

limitations: This record provides a general overview. Specific requirements vary significantly by state cinema regulation acts and local municipal norms.
Multiplex licensing may have additional conditions (parking, accessibility, emergency systems) not detailed here.
Entertainment tax implications and GST on cinema tickets are not covered.
The record does not cover temporary or touring cinema exhibition permits.
Digital projection and OTT screening venue requirements may differ from traditional cinema licensing.
The time and cost to obtain individual prerequisite NOCs are not modelled as separate services here.

review.reviewReason: Central act framework is reviewed but state-specific cinema regulation rules and current fee structures need per-state verification.
nextReviewTrigger: Amendments to the Cinematograph Act or state cinema regulation acts.
Changes in fire safety or structural safety norms for public assembly venues.
Introduction of unified online cinema licensing portal by states.
Changes in multiplex policy or single-screen revival policies by state governments.
